doc.title: Frank Wess — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: U Street and the changed D.C. neighborhood and clubs
summary: Wess describes U Street as transformed since desegregation, with few black businesses left; they discuss the Lincoln, Howard, and Bohemian Caverns.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Can you describe when you do go back, and maybe it’s a situation like for that filming. What’s your experience when you walk down, say, U Street today?

Well, it’s totally different. Washington has changed so much. U Street used to be in the black neighborhood but now it’s not, you know? Everything is everywhere and there are not many black businesses left there now. I don’t know if that industrial bank is still there, that was a black bank at 11th and U. I don’t know if it is still there are not. All the things have changed since they…you know, had that…what do they call it? I’ve forgotten…desegregation, or whatever it was. There are no more black neighborhoods in Washington. So U Street is…
So it almost seems kind of foreign?
It is because there’s nothing that what it was.
That’s too bad. Some of the remaining businesses, like the clubs, you know like the Lincoln Theatre, are still operating.
The Lincoln Theatre has always been there. You know, the Lincoln Theatre and the Republic, and the Howard Theatre is still there.
And the Caverns, have you been to the Bohemian Caverns since they kind of reopened it.
No, I haven’t been in there but I hear its still operating.

Yeah, I hear that the actual basement part is still, pretty much, as it was. But, I think they started out trying to do a lot of jazz things when they re-opened it but I don’t know how that has shaken out.
Yeah, I haven’t heard anything about it. Ken Kimery: They’ve actually been doing quite well.
Oh good! Good! Ken Kimery: Ron Carter has been in there. So, they’ve been making great strides.
I don’t know any jazz groups that have played there recently, you know?
Ken was just saying Ron Carter was there.
Oh he was there? I didn’t hear about it. I don’t have any connection with Washington other than Billy Taylor, you know? He’s so different, you know? To me, nothing is ever quite right. It's close.
